# S1. Purpose and estimand

The outbreak time series used in the outbreak-response immunization (ORI) analysis contain
predominantly **suspected** typhoid cases. Suspected-case definitions are designed for sensitive
outbreak detection and may include patients with other febrile illnesses. Consequently, not every
reported suspected case represents vaccine-preventable *Salmonella enterica* serovar Typhi
infection.

We define the positive predictive value (PPV) of the suspected clinical case definition in setting
$o$ as

$$
\pi_o = P(D=1 \mid C=1, o),
$$

where $D=1$ denotes latent true typhoid and $C=1$ denotes satisfaction of the study's suspected-case
definition. This quantity is the prevalence of true typhoid among suspected cases, not the PPV of
blood culture. It is setting-dependent because it reflects the local ratio of typhoid to other
febrile illnesses, the breadth of the clinical definition, care-seeking, and surveillance practice.

The purpose of this analysis was to propagate uncertainty in $\pi_o$ into estimates of absolute true
typhoid cases averted, morbidity, treatment costs, and cases averted per vaccine dose. This targeted
evidence synthesis was constructed as an observation model for the ORI analysis. It was **not** a
systematic review of all typhoid clinical case definitions; a broader PRISMA-DTA review is planned as
a separate study.

# S2. Evidence inputs

## S2.1 Paired blood- and bone-marrow-culture studies

Blood culture is highly specific but incompletely sensitive, so culture positivity alone cannot be
equated with the PPV of a clinical definition. We used nine historic studies, consolidated from
Mogasale et al. (2016), in which the same suspected patients received both blood culture and
bone-marrow culture. These studies supplied the four joint outcomes BC+BM+, BC+BM-, BC-BM+, and
BC-BM-. Together they included `r sum(hist$n_tested_both)` paired observations.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-paired-evidence
#| tbl-cap: "Paired blood- and bone-marrow-culture evidence used in the latent-class model."
paired_show <- data.frame(
  Study = hist$study,
  Location = hist$location,
  `BC+ BM+` = hist$a_BCpos_BMpos,
  `BC+ BM-` = hist$b_BCpos_BMneg,
  `BC- BM+` = hist$c_BCneg_BMpos,
  `BC- BM-` = hist$d_BCneg_BMneg,
  N = hist$n_tested_both,
  `Blood volume used (mL)` = fmt(hist$blood_volume_used_mL, 1),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(paired_show)
```

Blood volume was not reported for Hirsowitz (1951) and was imputed at the median of the reported
study volumes (4 mL). Gasem (1995) cultured 3 mL and 10 mL blood volumes, but its available
aggregate $2\times2$ table could not be separated by volume, so the consolidated analysis used 3
mL. Wain (2008) reported separate paired comparisons for 5 mL and 15 mL blood cultures; the analysis
used its 5 mL comparison. Vallenas (1985) was excluded because its primary report supplied
only marginal blood- and bone-marrow-culture yields, while the joint cells reported by Mogasale et
al. were internally inconsistent with those marginals and did not establish a defensible
both-negative cell. The remaining volume decisions were treated as data-quality limitations rather
than known without error.

## S2.2 Blood-volume information

The prior for the effect of blood volume on blood-culture sensitivity was informed by the
meta-regression of Antillón et al. (2018), which demonstrated increasing sensitivity with cultured
blood volume. The model used a Normal(0.36, 0.15) prior for the log-volume slope. The Antillón
study-level observations informed this slope prior rather than entering the paired-test likelihood
as independent patients.

## S2.3 Community outbreak observations

The community layer estimates the positive predictive value of the clinical *suspected*-case
definition — the probability $\pi_o = P(\text{true typhoid}\mid\text{suspected})$ among all
suspected cases in outbreak $o$ — because the renewal impact model scales suspected-case incidence
curves rather than culture-confirmed counts. Admissibility for this estimand, rather than culture
positivity itself, governed selection: a report had to provide a syndromic suspected-case
denominator, a blood-culture-specific tested count drawn from that denominator, and a
blood-culture-positive count.

Candidate outbreaks were pooled from two systematic reviews of typhoid outbreaks. Koh et al. (2025)
contributed its outbreaks with usable time series together with reports it had excluded for lacking
time-series data, which we re-screened specifically for PPV eligibility; Appiah et al. (2020)
contributed further records not already represented. After de-duplication at the publication level
this yielded 107 candidate outbreak records. Primary full texts were audited where retrievable;
review tables, indexed abstracts, and existing project extractions were used for the remainder, and
records whose structure could not be resolved were held pending rather than assumed eligible.

A record entered the primary community model only if it satisfied all of: (1) a suspected-case count
defined by a clinical case definition independently of culture result, rather than a confirmed-case
or isolate series; (2) a blood-culture-specific tested count, not pooled across blood, stool, urine,
or bone marrow; (3) a blood-culture-positive count from the same cultured subset; and (4) outbreak
independence, that is, a single observation per epidemic. Small samples were retained where the
denominator and the culture-selection mechanism were sound, with uncertainty propagated through the
binomial likelihood rather than removed by a fixed sample-size threshold. Small records were placed
in sensitivity analysis or excluded when they also had unresolved or inferred denominators, unclear
specimen scope, or poorly characterized culture selection.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-community-selection
#| tbl-cap: "Selection of community outbreak observations for PPV estimation."
sel_role <- community_audit$ppv_model_role
community_selection <- data.frame(
  Stage = c(
    "Candidate outbreak records (Koh 2025 review + no-time-series re-screen + Appiah 2020)",
    "Excluded from PPV modeling",
    "Retained for sensitivity analysis only",
    "Awaiting primary-source retrieval",
    "Included in the primary community PPV model"),
  n = c(nrow(community_audit),
        sum(sel_role == "exclude from PPV modeling"),
        sum(sel_role == "sensitivity analysis only"),
        sum(sel_role == "not yet: source reconstruction or retrieval required"),
        sum(included)),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(community_selection)
```

Exclusions fell into recurring classes: confirmed-only or culture-defined case series with no
independent syndromic denominator; pooled-specimen or non-blood tested denominators, for which
positivity does not equal blood-culture PPV; hospital, phase-specific, or severity-gated frames whose
estimand differs from all suspected outbreak cases; and off-target records such as genomic
isolate-characterization or water-sanitation survey papers carrying no testing flow. A full-text
reconstruction audit of the records whose summary counts were ambiguous confirmed that none yielded
an admissible blood-culture-specific triple—the dominant failure modes being pooled-specimen
confirmation and absent tested denominators. Qamar (2018) yielded a flagged pair retained for
sensitivity analysis; Al-Sanouri (2008) remained excluded because its tested denominator was inferred
rather than reported. Five records remained pending source reconstruction or retrieval.

The 107 records resolved to 103 independence groups. Three duplicate families accounted for the
difference: the Limpitikul 2014 period-1, period-2, and total records; the two Baddam 2012 records; and
the overlapping N'Cho 2019 and Poncin 2022 reports of the 2017--2018 Harare outbreak. All Limpitikul
and Baddam observations were excluded. For Harare, N'Cho supplied the only compatible
blood-culture-tested denominator and was retained; Poncin lacked a corresponding tested denominator
and was excluded from the likelihood. Where the primary paper permitted, blood-culture counts were
corrected at extraction to their blood-specific values—for example, Neil 2012 as 19/54 rather than
the pooled 25/63, and Kabwama 2017 as 56/364 rather than a stale 51/364.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-community-evidence
#| tbl-cap: "Community outbreak evidence used to estimate suspected-case-definition PPV."
comm_show <- merge(
  community_tight[, c("study", "country", "year", "suspected", "tested", "confirmed_cx", "positivity")],
  pi_est[, c("study", "pi_med", "pi_lo", "pi_hi")], by = "study", sort = FALSE)
comm_show <- comm_show[match(community_tight$study, comm_show$study), ]
comm_table <- data.frame(
  Study = comm_show$study,
  Country = comm_show$country,
  Year = comm_show$year,
  Suspected = comm_show$suspected,
  Cultured = comm_show$tested,
  `Culture positive` = comm_show$confirmed_cx,
  `Observed positivity` = fmt(comm_show$positivity, 3),
  `Latent true-typhoid PPV, median [90% CrI]` =
    interval(comm_show$pi_med, comm_show$pi_lo, comm_show$pi_hi, 2),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(comm_table)
```

The eight included outbreaks span three verification-adjustment grades — four major (Aye 2004,
Neil 2012, Kabwama 2017, N'Cho 2019), one moderate (Makungo 2020), and three negligible or low
(Hu 2022, Dhadwal 2008, Swaddiwudhipong 2001) — reflecting how far each cultured subset departs from
a random sample of all suspected cases. Six derive from the Koh 2025 review; Dhadwal 2008 and
Swaddiwudhipong 2001 were recovered from its no-time-series re-screen. Because blood volume was not
reported in any of the eight, the primary fit assumed 5 mL and varied this assumption from 3 to
10 mL as its principal structural sensitivity.

Two limitations are quantified rather than assumed. The verification-adjustment grade enters a
selection sub-model whose magnitude is prior-dominated (Section S5.4), and the suspected-case
denominator is not always the same population as the renewal time-series curve it scales, as
reported in the denominator-frame alignment table (Section S5). One retained anchor carries a
specimen caveat: N'Cho 2019's 74/286 is reported as "cultures processed," not disaggregated to
blood culture, under a blood, stool, or rectal-swab confirmation definition. It is retained as a
genuine tested and positive pair within its 583-patient hospital frame, with a leave-N'Cho-out
sensitivity analysis to bound its influence.

# S3. Latent-class model

## S3.1 Blood-culture sensitivity

For paired study $s$, blood-culture sensitivity was modeled as

$$
\operatorname{logit}(Se_{BC,s}) = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1\log(V_s) + \tau u_s,
\qquad u_s\sim\operatorname{Normal}(0,1),
$$

where $V_s$ is blood volume, $\alpha_0$ is the sensitivity level, $\alpha_1$ is the volume slope,
and $\tau$ is residual between-study heterogeneity. Bone-marrow sensitivity ($Se_{BM}$) was
estimated rather than fixed, acknowledging that bone marrow is a better but imperfect reference.

## S3.2 Paired-test likelihood

Let $\phi_s=P(D=1\mid C=1,s)$ be the latent true-typhoid prevalence among the hospital-referred
suspected patients in paired study $s$. Under conditional independence of blood and bone-marrow
culture given latent disease status, the four cell probabilities were

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_{++} &= \phi_s Se_{BC,s}Se_{BM} +(1-\phi_s)(1-Sp_{BC})(1-Sp_{BM}),\\
p_{+-} &= \phi_s Se_{BC,s}(1-Se_{BM}) +(1-\phi_s)(1-Sp_{BC})Sp_{BM},\\
p_{-+} &= \phi_s (1-Se_{BC,s})Se_{BM} +(1-\phi_s)Sp_{BC}(1-Sp_{BM}),\\
p_{--} &= \phi_s (1-Se_{BC,s})(1-Se_{BM}) +(1-\phi_s)Sp_{BC}Sp_{BM}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The observed four-cell vector followed a multinomial distribution. The paired layer identifies the
sensitivity of both cultures and the study-specific hospital PPV without treating either culture as
a perfect gold standard.

## S3.3 Community likelihood

For community outbreak $o$, let $N_o$ be all suspected cases, $n_o$ the number cultured, and $k_o$
the number culture-positive. PPV among all suspected cases was modeled hierarchically:

$$
\operatorname{logit}(\pi_o)=\mu_\pi+\sigma_\pi z_o,\qquad z_o\sim\operatorname{Normal}(0,1).
$$

To represent preferential verification, $q_{1o}$ and $q_{0o}$ denote the probabilities of culture
among true-typhoid and non-typhoid suspected cases. Their log-odds difference was

$$
\delta_o=\operatorname{logit}(q_{1o})-\operatorname{logit}(q_{0o})
=\mu_\delta+\beta_{bias}B_o+\sigma_\delta z_{\delta o},
$$

where $B_o\in\{0,1,2\}$ is the prespecified audit grade for low, moderate, or major verification
concern. Counts $(k_o,n_o-k_o,N_o-n_o)$ followed a multinomial distribution for culture-positive,
culture-negative, and untested suspected cases. Thus, both testing fraction and positivity inform
the model, while true cases may be preferentially cultured. Structured priors remain necessary
because selection and population PPV are not identified by these counts alone.

## S3.4 Priors and computation

```{r}
#| label: tbl-priors
#| tbl-cap: "Priors used in the final latent-class model."
priors <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Blood-culture intercept, alpha0", "Log-volume slope, alpha1",
                "Between-study Se SD, tau", "Bone-marrow sensitivity",
                "Culture specificities", "Hospital PPV, phi_s",
                "Population logit-PPV mean, mu_pi", "Between-outbreak PPV SD, sigma_pi",
                "Baseline selection, mu_delta", "Bias-grade slope, beta_bias",
                "Residual selection SD, sigma_delta", "Non-typhoid testing logit, logit(q0)"),
  Prior = c("Normal(0, 1.5)", "Normal(0.36, 0.15)", "half-Normal(0, 1)",
            "Beta(12, 2)", "Beta(200, 1)", "Beta(1, 1)",
            "Normal(logit(0.25), 1)", "half-Normal(0, 0.8)", "Normal(0, 0.5)",
            "Normal+(0.5, 0.4)", "half-Normal(0, 0.5)",
            "Normal(logit observed testing fraction, 1)"),
  Rationale = c("Weakly informative sensitivity level", "Antillon-informed volume effect",
                "Residual sensitivity heterogeneity", "High but imperfect sensitivity",
                "A positive culture is highly specific", "Local paired-study prevalence",
                "Weakly informative population PPV", "Genuine between-outbreak PPV variation",
                "No baseline enrichment favored", "Higher audit concern permits enrichment",
                "Unmeasured selection heterogeneity", "Anchors testing to observed coverage"),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(priors)
```

The model was fitted in Stan using four chains, 1,500 warm-up iterations and 1,500 retained
iterations per chain, seed 2026, target acceptance probability 0.98, and maximum tree depth 12.
Posterior summaries are medians and 90% credible intervals (CrIs).
Structural selection sensitivities used two chains with 800 warm-up and 800 retained iterations per
chain. Their maximum $\widehat R$ was `r fmt(max(selection_sens$max_rhat), 3)`; the main four-chain
fit's maximum $\widehat R$ is reported separately below.

# S4. Model validation and diagnostics

The final fit produced `r diag$divergences` divergent transitions; the maximum rank-normalized
$\widehat R$ was `r fmt(diag$max_rhat, 3)`, and the minimum bulk effective sample size was
`r fmt(diag$min_ess_bulk, 0)`. These diagnostics indicated satisfactory sampling.

Simulation studies evaluated recovery of the shared sensitivity parameters and local PPVs. The
identifiable parameters were recovered with the generating values inside their 90% CrIs under the
tested design. A single-test demonstration reproduced the expected PPV--sensitivity ridge: PPV and
blood-culture sensitivity were individually weakly identified, while their product was precise.
The paired-test layer removed this ridge. An earlier severity offset was not identified because the
paired blood/bone-marrow evidence came from hospital populations and no comparable paired evidence
exists for ambulatory disease. The final model therefore omitted a severity term and transferred
blood-culture sensitivity through observed or assumed blood volume plus residual heterogeneity.

In a stress test, data generated with positive conditional dependence between blood and
bone-marrow culture but fitted under independence increased estimated blood-culture sensitivity by
approximately 0.08 and decreased PPV by approximately 0.08. Conditional independence is therefore a
directional limitation: shared culture failure, for example after antibiotic exposure, could make
the primary model overestimate sensitivity and underestimate PPV.

# S5. Results

## S5.1 Culture accuracy

```{r}
#| label: tbl-accuracy-results
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior estimates of culture-accuracy parameters."
labels <- c(
  Se_BC_2mL = "Blood-culture sensitivity at 2 mL",
  Se_BC_5mL = "Blood-culture sensitivity at 5 mL",
  Se_BC_10mL = "Blood-culture sensitivity at 10 mL",
  Se_BM = "Bone-marrow-culture sensitivity",
  Sp_BC = "Blood-culture specificity",
  alpha1 = "Log-volume slope",
  tau = "Between-study SD")
acc <- pars[match(names(labels), pars$param), ]
acc_table <- data.frame(
  Parameter = unname(labels),
  `Median [90% CrI]` = interval(acc$med, acc[[3]], acc[[4]], 2),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(acc_table)
```

At the assumed 5 mL community blood volume, blood culture detected an estimated 0.65 of latent true
typhoid infections. Sensitivity increased with cultured volume, while estimated bone-marrow
sensitivity was approximately 0.92. Thus, raw culture positivity materially underestimated the
proportion of suspected patients with true typhoid.

```{r}
#| label: fig-se-volume
#| fig-cap: "Posterior blood-culture sensitivity by cultured blood volume. The line and band show the posterior median and 90% CrI; points show raw paired-study detection proportions."
#| out-width: "85%"
knitr::include_graphics(path("latent_class_ppv/figures/fig_final_se_volume.png"))
```

## S5.2 Hospital and community PPV

Hospital-referred PPVs across the nine paired studies ranged from `r fmt(min(phi$phi_med), 2)` to
`r fmt(max(phi$phi_med), 2)` (median `r fmt(median(phi$phi_med), 2)`). Community outbreak PPV was
heterogeneous across `r nrow(pi_est)` audited, independence-checked observations, ranging from
`r fmt(min(pi_est$pi_med), 2)` to `r fmt(max(pi_est$pi_med), 2)`. These are local estimates and
should not be interpreted as a universal PPV for typhoid surveillance. In particular, N'Cho 2019
is the sole diagnostic-yield observation retained from the 2017--2018 Harare outbreak; Poncin 2022
summarizes overlapping historical counts but supplies no blood-culture-tested denominator.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppv-setting
#| fig-cap: "Posterior PPV of the suspected clinical definition in hospital-referred and community outbreak populations. PPVs are study-specific; intervals are 90% CrIs."
#| out-width: "90%"
knitr::include_graphics(path("latent_class_ppv/figures/fig_final_ppv.png"))
```

The fitted population median PPV was
`r interval(pars$med[pars$param == "pi_population_median"], pars$lo.5.[pars$param == "pi_population_median"], pars$hi.95.[pars$param == "pi_population_median"])`,
and the genuine between-outbreak logit-scale SD was
`r interval(pars$med[pars$param == "sigma_pi"], pars$lo.5.[pars$param == "sigma_pi"], pars$hi.95.[pars$param == "sigma_pi"])`.
The audit-grade selection coefficient was positive:
`r interval(pars$med[pars$param == "beta_bias"], pars$lo.5.[pars$param == "beta_bias"], pars$hi.95.[pars$param == "beta_bias"])`.
This should not be interpreted as data-driven evidence for enrichment: the selection hyperparameters
changed little from their priors, unlike the clearly updated between-outbreak PPV SD.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-selection
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior culture-selection probabilities among true and non-typhoid suspected cases."
selection_table <- data.frame(
  Study=selection_est$study,
  `Selection log-OR, median [90% CrI]`=interval(selection_est$delta_med, selection_est$delta_lo, selection_est$delta_hi),
  `P(cultured | non-typhoid)`=interval(selection_est$q0_med, selection_est$q0_lo, selection_est$q0_hi),
  `P(cultured | true typhoid)`=interval(selection_est$q1_med, selection_est$q1_lo, selection_est$q1_hi),
  check.names=FALSE)
kable(selection_table)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hospital-ppv
#| tbl-cap: "Study-specific hospital PPV estimates from the paired-test layer."
phi_table <- data.frame(
  Study = phi$study,
  `Blood volume used (mL)` = fmt(phi$vol_mL, 1),
  `PPV, median [90% CrI]` = interval(phi$phi_med, phi$phi_lo, phi$phi_hi, 2),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(phi_table)
```

## S5.3 Sensitivity to assumed outbreak blood volume

```{r}
#| label: tbl-volume-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Community PPV sensitivity to assumed blood volume in outbreak surveillance."
vs_table <- data.frame(
  `Assumed blood volume (mL)` = volsens$assumed_blood_volume_mL,
  Study = volsens$study,
  `Blood-culture sensitivity` = fmt(volsens$Se_BC_median, 2),
  `PPV median` = fmt(volsens$pi_median, 2),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(vs_table)
```

Increasing assumed blood volume raised estimated blood-culture sensitivity and correspondingly
lowered inferred PPV. The direction was expected from the approximate identity
$\text{positivity}\approx\pi Se_{BC}$; the qualitative separation between hospital and community
settings was unchanged.

## S5.4 Sensitivity to selection assumptions

The selection decomposition was examined under no enrichment; skeptical, base, and permissive
enrichment priors; binary rather than ordinal audit grades; and no grade effect. These are structural
sensitivity analyses, not data-supported model rankings.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-selection-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity of inferred PPV and ORI impact to selection priors and audit-grade coding."
ss_one <- selection_sens[!duplicated(selection_sens$scenario), ]
ss_major <- selection_sens[selection_sens$study == "Kabwama 2017", c("scenario", "deflation_med")]
ss <- merge(ss_one, ss_major, by="scenario", suffixes=c("", "_major"))
ss <- merge(ss, ppv_selection_sens, by="scenario")
scenario_labels <- c(no_enrichment="No enrichment", skeptical="Skeptical priors",
                     base="Base priors", permissive="Permissive priors",
                     binary_grade="Binary grade", no_grade="No grade effect")
ss_table <- data.frame(
  Scenario=unname(scenario_labels[ss$scenario]),
  `Population PPV median`=fmt(ss$pi_population_med, 2),
  `Predictive PPV, median [90% interval]`=interval(ss$pi_new_med, ss$pi_new_lo, ss$pi_new_hi),
  `Kabwama population/tested PPV ratio`=fmt(ss$deflation_med_major, 2),
  `True cases averted`=fmt(ss$true_cases_averted, 0),
  `Observed suspected-case reduction (%)`=fmt(ss$observed_pct_reduction, 1),
  check.names=FALSE)
kable(ss_table)
```

Across these assumptions, estimated true cases averted ranged from
`r fmt(min(ppv_selection_sens$true_cases_averted), 0)` to
`r fmt(max(ppv_selection_sens$true_cases_averted), 0)`. This spread is consequential and is driven
by the analyst-specified enrichment prior and grade encoding; the data do not select among these
scenarios.

# S6. Propagation into the ORI analysis

Posterior PPV draws were propagated jointly with vaccine-effectiveness and campaign-timing draws.
All `r nrow(pi_est)` audited anchors use their study-specific $\pi_o$ posterior when the ORI dataset
contains the same study identifier. For outbreaks without direct PPV data, the current implementation
draws an outbreak-specific value from the fitted logit-normal population distribution using each
draw's $\mu_\pi$ and $\sigma_\pi$. This propagates genuine fitted between-outbreak heterogeneity.
Preferential selection
into blood culture is represented jointly through the tested, test-negative, test-positive, and
untested counts, conditional on the prespecified audit bias grade.

The testing-frame denominator used to estimate an anchor's PPV is not necessarily the same
population or time window as the renewal incidence curve. The audit below makes that transport step
explicit. A numerical mismatch is not repaired by the selection model and is not included in the
selection-prior sensitivity range.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-denominator-frame-audit
#| tbl-cap: "Alignment of Stan suspected-case testing frames with canonical renewal time-series totals."
denom_table <- data.frame(
  Study=denominator_audit$study,
  `Stan testing frame`=denominator_audit$stan_testing_frame_n,
  `Canonical curve total`=ifelse(is.na(denominator_audit$renewal_curve_sum), "No matching curve",
                                 fmt(denominator_audit$renewal_curve_sum, 0)),
  `Used in renewal model`=ifelse(denominator_audit$renewal_model_included, "Yes", "No"),
  Alignment=denominator_audit$frame_alignment,
  check.names=FALSE)
kable(denom_table)
```

Two observation regimes are available:

1. **Multiplicative regime:** $I_t=\pi S_t$, where $S_t$ is suspected incidence and $I_t$ is latent
   true typhoid incidence. With constant $\pi$, percentage reduction and reconstructed transmission
   are invariant, while absolute cases, YLDs, costs, and cases per dose are scaled by $\pi$.
2. **Additive-background regime:** $S_t=I_t+B_t$, where the non-typhoid febrile background is assumed
   constant over the outbreak. The implementation sets $B=(1-\pi)\overline S$, truncates negative
   $I_t$, and renormalizes the true-typhoid curve to sum to $\pi\sum_tS_t$. Vaccination acts on $I_t$
   only, so background illness dilutes the percentage change observable in suspected surveillance.

The current ORI configuration uses the additive-background regime. At a second additive level, true
typhoid is decomposed as $I_t=X_t+P_t$, where $X_t$ is background/common-source typhoid and
$P_t=R_t^P\sum_{u\ge1}w_uI_{t-u}$ is propagated typhoid. Under vaccination, the remaining
susceptibility multiplier $q_t$ acts on both components:
$X_t^v=q_tX_t$ and
$P_t^v=q_tR_t^P\sum_{u\ge1}w_uI_{t-u}^v$. Other febrile illness remains fixed, whereas propagated
typhoid additionally declines through transmission feedback.

The former calculation
$A_\theta=\theta A_{\mathrm{static}}+(1-\theta)A_{\mathrm{renewal}}$ averages completed outcomes
and is retained only as a historical comparator. In the primary model, the source fraction
$\theta$ allocates baseline true-typhoid incidence *within* the shared additive recursion; it is
informed by field-epidemiologic source classification because its level was not identifiable from
curve shape alone.

Because the other-febrile background curve is not directly observed, the multiplicative
observation regime should be reported as a structural sensitivity analysis. Deaths attributed to
typhoid were not multiplied by PPV; deaths/YLLs were treated as already disease-specific, whereas
non-fatal case counts, YLDs, treatment costs, and AMR case counts were adjusted.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ppv-effect
#| tbl-cap: "Effect of PPV adjustment in the current ORI base-case run."
effect_table <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Summed per-outbreak median cases averted",
               "Pooled true-typhoid percentage reduction",
               "Pooled percentage reduction observable in suspected surveillance"),
  `Without PPV adjustment` = c(
    fmt(ppv_effect$suspected_naive[1], 0),
    paste0(fmt(ppv_effect$suspected_naive[2], 1), "%"),
    "Not applicable"),
  `With PPV adjustment` = c(
    fmt(ppv_effect$true_typhoid[1], 0),
    paste0(fmt(ppv_effect$true_typhoid[2], 1), "%"),
    paste0(fmt(ppv_effect$true_typhoid[3], 1), "%")),
  check.names = FALSE)
kable(effect_table)
```

PPV adjustment reduced the estimated absolute vaccine-preventable burden substantially. Under the
additive observation model, it also distinguished the reduction in latent true typhoid from the
smaller change expected in all-cause suspected-case surveillance.

In paired base-case simulations, the additive source-plus-propagated model averted
`r fmt(source_comparison$additive_cases_median, 0)` true-typhoid cases
(`r fmt(source_comparison$additive_cases_p025, 0)`--`r fmt(source_comparison$additive_cases_p975, 0)`)
and reduced true typhoid by `r fmt(source_comparison$additive_true_pct_median, 1)`%. The historical
$\theta$-weighted version reduced true typhoid by
`r fmt(source_comparison$historical_weighted_true_pct_median, 1)`%. The paired difference was
`r fmt(source_comparison$delta_true_pp_median, 1)` percentage points
(`r fmt(source_comparison$delta_true_pp_p025, 1)` to
`r fmt(source_comparison$delta_true_pp_p975, 1)`). The primary model produced a
`r fmt(source_comparison$additive_observed_pct_median, 1)`% reduction in suspected-case
surveillance. All `r nrow(source_validation)` prespecified mass-balance, endpoint, non-negativity,
and pairing checks passed.

# S7. Assumptions and limitations

1. **Targeted evidence base.** The model used a deliberately selected evidence set suitable for the
   ORI observation model, not a completed systematic review of clinical-definition accuracy or
   positivity. Numerical estimates should be updated when the planned systematic evidence synthesis
   is complete.
2. **Community anchors.** `r nrow(pi_est)` independence-checked outbreak observations directly
   informed community PPV. The predictive distribution remains sensitive to case-definition and
   testing-selection heterogeneity across these studies.
3. **Representativeness of cultured patients.** The selection layer adjusts for preferential
   culture of true cases using testing fractions and audit bias grades, but this structure is
   **prior-dominated**: the available aggregate counts do not identify population PPV separately
   from enrichment into culture. Results remain sensitive to its priors and grade coding, as the
   reported structural sensitivity sweep demonstrates, and to unmeasured selection factors
   such as severity, antibiotics, laboratory capacity, and clinician judgment.
4. **Blood volume.** Community blood volume was assumed rather than observed. The 3--10 mL sensitivity
   analysis quantifies this uncertainty but cannot replace outbreak-specific collection volumes.
5. **Denominator-frame transport.** Several local PPV anchors use a suspected-case testing frame
   that differs from the canonical renewal curve in population, time window, or total count. The
   1,511--2,277 selection-prior range conditions on those frame choices and therefore does not
   quantify this additional uncertainty. N'Cho is especially consequential (583 in the hospital
   testing frame versus 2,744 cases in the canonical curve).
6. **Conditional independence.** Shared blood- and bone-marrow-culture failure could cause the model
   to overestimate sensitivity and underestimate PPV.
7. **Historic data quality.** One blood volume was imputed, two studies combined multiple volumes,
   and one both-negative cell was reconstructed from the reported total.
8. **Definition heterogeneity.** Clinical definitions differed across studies. The present model
   estimates setting-specific PPV but does not yet include definition stringency as a covariate.
9. **Background structure.** The additive observation regime assumes a constant non-typhoid
   background. Seasonal or outbreak-correlated alternative febrile illness would violate this
   assumption.
10. **Ratio versus absolute outcomes.** Under multiplicative scaling, PPV affects absolute burden but
   cancels from percentage reductions and reconstructed $R_t$. Under the additive regime it also
   changes epidemic shape and observed percentage reduction, making its structural assumptions more
   consequential.
11. **Source-fraction structure.** The source fraction is externally informed and represents an
    allocation of true-typhoid incidence inside the renewal recursion, not an identified causal
    decomposition. The paired historical weighted result is a structural comparator rather than an
    uncertainty bound.

# S8. Reproducibility

The final latent-class model is implemented in `latent_class_ppv/stan/model_final.stan` and fitted by
`latent_class_ppv/run_final.R`. The fit uses seed 2026 and writes posterior draws, parameter tables,
diagnostics, sensitivity tables, and figures under `latent_class_ppv/outputs`,
`latent_class_ppv/tables`, and `latent_class_ppv/figures`. The ORI propagation is implemented in
`renewal/R/ppv.R` and `renewal/R/renewal_core.R`, configured in `renewal/config.yml`, and compared
with the historical weighted formulation by `source_decomposition/run_source_decomposition.R`.

To reproduce the PPV fit and this supplement from the repository root:

```text
Rscript latent_class_ppv/run_final.R
Rscript renewal/run_analysis.R
Rscript source_decomposition/run_source_decomposition.R
Rscript revision/run_selection_sensitivity.R
quarto render revision/ppv_supplement.qmd --to html
quarto render revision/ppv_supplement.qmd --to docx --output ppv_supplement_selection_sensitivity.docx
Move-Item ppv_supplement_selection_sensitivity.docx revision/ppv_supplement_selection_sensitivity.docx -Force
```

The canonical DOCX deliverable is `revision/ppv_supplement_selection_sensitivity.docx`.
`revision/ppv_supplement.docx` is a superseded locked artifact and should not be distributed.
